newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solid UCB still only a 'hold' - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Solid UCB still only a 'hold' - analysts.

text.p: Analysts are cautious about shares in Belgian chemicals and drugs group UCB, due to report 1996 earnings after the bourse close on Wednesday, saying the stock is fully valued and its upside scope limited.
Currently priced at 94,300 Belgian francs each, the share is among the most expensive ones in absolute terms on the main forward market of the Brussels bourse.
In relative terms, the stock is not cheap either even after a one-week correction which lobbed 3.6 percent off the UCB share price, but only one percent off the Bel-20 index .BFX.
The correction, which came as the share hit overbought territory last week, still leaves the share up 16 percent since the start of 1997, while the Bel-20 has gained only 10 percent.

Analyst Sandra Vandersmissen at Generale bank said the share was a 'hold.' She might consider buying again once the price/ earnings ratio reached 24 or 25, down from the current 27.5. UCB's strength is in part due to a tight market, analysts said, citing this as one of the reasons why the share is rated a 'hold'. In terms of book value per share, estimated at 20,500 francs, the stock is expensive.
Its price to book ratio is also above the market's average.
Analysts say the stock could easily be split four for one and still trade above book per value per share, but the company has said it will not consider a share split in the near term.
Buying interest has also been driven by solid results, though, and good prospects, analysts said.

Ordinary profit -- excluding exceptionals -- is forecast to have reached five billion to 5.5 billion Belgian francs. In the first half of 1996 UCB had already chalked up profits matching the 4.25 billion recorded for the full year 1995.

One analyst predicted the pharma sector would have three to 3.3 billion francs in current profits with two-thirds coming from star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec which was launched successfully in the U.S. in 1996.
Registration in Japan is expected for the second half this year and sales are due to start next year. Zyrtec is expected to be launched in Belgium in 1998.

In chemicals, current profits are seen nudging up to about 1.2 billion from 1.17 billion in 1995, he said. In the high added value films sector, current profit is forecast to reach about 500 million francs after 417 million in 1995.
Earnings per share (EPS) including exceptionals are expected to rise from 2,243 francs in 1995 to between 2,750 to 3,000 francs for 1996 and 3,375 to 3,400 in 1997.
Dividend per share is put at 700 to 750 francs for 1996, up from 600 in 1995, and 800 to 825 in 1997.

Generale Bank's Vandersmissen expected the dividend to be 750 francs on the assumption UCB would maintain its pay-out ratio. In addition, "they got a lot of cash last year", she added, commenting on the forecast dividend rise.
